cases.description: Should trigger: simplify a working but messy function
cases.input: This function works but has 7 levels of nesting and unclear variable names. Simplify it without changing behavior.
cases.expect: Enter the simplification process: understand the code, apply structured simplifications, verify tests still pass
assertions: Begins by understanding what the code does before making changes
Identifies specific structural complexity (nesting, naming)
Preserves all inputs, outputs, and edge cases
Verifies existing tests pass after changes

cases.description: Should trigger: reduce cognitive load in reviewed code
cases.input: In this PR the conditional logic is deeply nested with multiple ternaries. Clean it up for readability.
cases.expect: Apply the simplification process to the specific code, prioritizing clarity over cleverness
assertions: Converts nested ternaries to clear conditional branches
Preserves all code paths and return values
Makes incremental, reviewable changes
Would a new team member understand this faster than the original?

cases.description: Should trigger: refactor after feature is done and tests pass
cases.input: The feature is shipped and all 142 tests pass but the implementation feels heavy. Make it simpler.
cases.expect: Apply after feature-complete refinement: identify over-engineering, remove dead code, consolidate duplication
assertions: Confirms tests pass before starting
Separates refactoring from feature work
Removes abstractions that are 'maybe useful later' but unused now
Runs tests again after each incremental change

cases.description: Should trigger: consolidate duplicated logic across files
cases.input: We have the same pagination logic copied across 4 different service files. Unify it.
cases.expect: Extract shared logic while keeping each call site's interface unchanged
assertions: Extracts duplicated logic into a single shared location
Preserves each call site's existing contract
Runs existing tests without modification
Documents what changed and why

cases.description: Should trigger: simplify code written under time pressure
cases.input: This was written during a hackathon. It works but the variable names don't make sense and there's dead code everywhere.
cases.expect: Apply systematic simplification: rename unclear names, remove dead code, flatten nesting
assertions: Renames variables to reflect their purpose
Removes dead code (commented-out blocks, unreachable branches)
Flattens unnecessarily nested logic
Preserves every existing code path

cases.description: Not trigger: code is already clean and readable
cases.input: This code looks fine to me. Should I run a linter on it?
cases.expect: Recognize that no simplification is needed and recommend appropriate tooling instead
assertions: Does not enter the simplification procedure
Suggests an automated formatter/linter if style is the concern
Does not create unnecessary diffs

cases.description: Not trigger: performance-critical code that should not be simplified
cases.input: This hot loop is already using SIMD intrinsics. Can you make it more readable?
cases.expect: Recognize that performance-critical code may justify complexity and advise against simplification
assertions: Warns that performance-critical code may need its existing complexity
Offers to comment/document instead of restructure
Defers to benchmarking results before changing

cases.description: Not trigger: user doesn't understand the code yet
cases.input: I don't really understand what this code does but it seems long. Shorten it.
cases.expect: Recognize that comprehension must precede simplification and advise understanding first
assertions: Refuses to simplify code not yet understood
Offers to explain the code first
References Chesterton's Fence principle
